Yellow russulas are thankfully uncommon. The yellow cap with white stem seperate it from all other Russulas beside claroflava. Association with oaks, no red-blackening flesh, and a white spore print will separate ochroleucoides from claroflava.
Look-Alikes: R. flavidus complex (3 spp.), have stems concolorous with cap; R. earliei complex (2 spp.), less yellow and have un-Russula like widely spaced gills; R. claroflava bruises red then black, is associated with birch and maybe conifers, and has an (E-F) pale ochre spore print.
Ecology: Mycorrhizal with oaks and maybe beech
Etymology: ochro - pale yellow, leuco - white, oides - resembling
Other Notes: A Russula you can actually ID... what more do you want?
